headline: Dhaka, Beijing to sign 15-17 bilateral instruments during PM's visit
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit Malaysia and China to discuss labor markets, ASEAN membership, and infrastructure funding.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to visit Malaysia on Sunday, June 21, marking his first official foreign trip since the formation of the government.
In Malaysia, the Prime Minister will meet with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to discuss opening labor markets, obtaining ASEAN membership, and establishing a free trade agreement.
Following the Malaysia visit, the Prime Minister will travel to China, where he will stay from June 23 to 26.
During the China visit, he will hold bilateral meetings with the Chinese Prime Minister on June 25 and President Xi Jinping on June 26.
Key discussions in China will focus on integrated river and water management, specifically the Teesta Multipurpose Project.
Foreign Advisor Humayun Kabir stated that Dhaka and Beijing will sign 13 memorandums of understanding, 2 agreements, 1 action plan, and 1 protocol.
The visit is also expected to increase military cooperation between the two nations.
The Prime Minister will be accompanied by a 27-member delegation, including the Foreign Minister and Information Minister.
caption:
Dhaka and Beijing are set to sign up to 17 bilateral instruments as PM Tarique Rahman embarks on his first official foreign visit.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to visit Malaysia on Sunday, June 21, marking his first official foreign trip since the formation of the government.

In Malaysia, the Prime Minister will meet with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to discuss opening labor markets, obtaining ASEAN membership, and establishing a free trade agreement.

Following the Malaysia visit, the Prime Minister will travel to China, where he will stay from June 23 to 26.

During the China visit, he will hold bilateral meetings with the Chinese Prime Minister on June 25 and President Xi Jinping on June 26.

Key discussions in China will focus on integrated river and water management, specifically the Teesta Multipurpose Project.

Foreign Advisor Humayun Kabir stated that Dhaka and Beijing will sign 13 memorandums of understanding, 2 agreements, 1 action plan, and 1 protocol.

The visit is also expected to increase military cooperation between the two nations.

The Prime Minister will be accompanied by a 27-member delegation, including the Foreign Minister and Information Minister.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Somoy News

headline_marked: 20 people blocked: [[BGB foils BSF push-in attempt]] at Chapainawabganj border
headline: 20 people blocked: BGB foils BSF push-in attempt at Chapainawabganj border
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh troopers blocked 20 individuals, including women and children, from entering the country through the Chouka border.
details: The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has turned back 20 people at the Chapainawabganj border after India's Border Security Force (BSF) reportedly tried to push them across late Friday night.
The attempt took place at the Chouka border in Shibganj Upazila, according to Mahananda Battalion 59 BGB Commanding Officer Lt Col Md Tajul Islam Chowdhury.
The group consisted of 11 men, five women, and four children. A BGB patrol team spotted the attempt and immediately blocked their entry into Bangladesh.
Following the resistance, the 20 individuals remained in the no-man's land on the Indian side of the border before the BSF took them back across the wire around noon on Saturday.
The identities and nationalities of the people involved, as well as how they arrived at the border, remain unknown.
Lt Col Tajul stated that the alertness of the patrol team made it possible to foil the attempt, and officials are continuing to investigate the details of the incident.
caption:
20 people, including women and children, were blocked from entering Bangladesh after a reported BSF push-in attempt.

The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has turned back 20 people at the Chapainawabganj border after India's Border Security Force (BSF) reportedly tried to push them across late Friday night.

The attempt took place at the Chouka border in Shibganj Upazila, according to Mahananda Battalion 59 BGB Commanding Officer Lt Col Md Tajul Islam Chowdhury.

The group consisted of 11 men, five women, and four children. A BGB patrol team spotted the attempt and immediately blocked their entry into Bangladesh.

Following the resistance, the 20 individuals remained in the no-man's land on the Indian side of the border before the BSF took them back across the wire around noon on Saturday.

The identities and nationalities of the people involved, as well as how they arrived at the border, remain unknown.

Lt Col Tajul stated that the alertness of the patrol team made it possible to foil the attempt, and officials are continuing to investigate the details of the incident.
